chunks: 4851 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr, from Abu Basir, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said:
"Li'an does not take place unless the man has consummated the marriage with his wife."

key_terms.اللِّعَانُ: li'an, the mutual invocation of curse between spouses in a legal marital dispute
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ: enters upon, meaning consummates the marriage
key_terms.يَقَعُ: takes place or becomes legally established

ai.seo_question: When does li'an become valid between a husband and wife in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal condition for the occurrence of li'an between spouses. It indicates that li'an is not established unless the husband has entered upon his wife, meaning the marriage has been consummated.
